chapter_title: A Slap from a Childhood Sweetheart

segments.title: A Slap from a Childhood Sweetheart
segments.content:
"Li Luo! You've gone too far! Apologize to the class monitor right now!"

"Yeah, Chanxi was kind enough to give you a last-minute cram session, and even if you didn't appreciate it, why did you have to push her?"

"Li Luo... um, maybe you shouldn't go play ball? After all, you still have the high school entrance exams tomorrow."

In a daze, Li Luo heard the noisy voices around him, his mind reeling with dizziness.

Then he snapped his eyes open, and the situation before him gradually came into focus.

He was on a sidewalk paved with uneven red and green bricks, a crooked utility pole stood nearby, and the narrow street was teeming with people, leaving only the area immediately around him somewhat empty.

A boy with ordinary looks and a fair complexion was standing in front of him, his face flushed red and filled with anger, looking utterly furious.

Behind this boy were two girls.

One of them, a plump girl with freckles on her cheeks, was helping another girl up from the ground, looking at him with a frown and an expression of disgust.

And next to them stood a big, burly, dark-skinned, and tall fellow who, despite his build, looked rather honest.

Li Luo blinked, recognizing them.

The furious but scholarly-looking, fair-skinned boy was Shao Heqi, his vice class monitor in junior high.

The big, honest guy standing nearby was Zhao Rongjun, a good buddy he grew up with.

As for the two girls behind them, the plump, freckled one was named Jin Yuting.

And the delicate, pitiable girl being helped up was his childhood sweetheart—Ying Chanxi.

In Li Luo's memory, this should be the day he and Ying Chanxi officially fell out.

From this day forward, though they remained neighbors, they never spoke another word to each other.

Not until he was in his thirties, at his lowest and most desperate, did he receive a transfer of 10,000 yuan from Ying Chanxi.

It had saved him from a pressing crisis.

But even so, it was hard for the two of them to ever return to the close relationship they had as children.

Unless...

"What did you just say?" Li Luo turned his head to look at Zhao Rongjun, his eyes frighteningly bright.

"Huh?" Zhao Rongjun was stunned, a little spooked by his gaze, and answered subconsciously, "Uh... don't go play ball?"

"No, I mean the next sentence."

"The next sentence?" Zhao Rongjun blinked, "The high school entrance exams tomorrow?"

After confirming this, Li Luo looked around again at the youthful and vibrant faces before him, then looked down at his own hands, and the junior high school uniform he was wearing...

It seemed like he... had really been reborn!

Just a moment ago, he had been calling Taobao customers "dear" one after another, begging them to leave a good review.

In the blink of an eye, he had returned to the summer of 2014, standing once again at the most important crossroads of his life.

*Pa.*

A crisp slap echoed lightly.

Zhao Rongjun's eyes widened as he covered one side of his face. He took a half step back, staring at Li Luo in shock. "Seriously, bro... you didn't have to slap me for that, did you?"

"Does it hurt?" Li Luo looked at him with a burning gaze.

"...A little."

"Then hit me back." Li Luo's tone was a little excited, and he eagerly offered his own cheek. "Go on, hit me."

"Ah, this..." Although Zhao Rongjun was tall and imposing, he was an honest kid at heart. He couldn't bring himself to do it, and he looked at Li Luo with a troubled expression.

But in the next second, a slender figure strode forward quickly, her arm swinging—

*Pa!*

A slap, much crisper than the last one, resounded through the air.

Li Luo's head turned at a 45-degree angle. He blinked, a bit stunned himself. A clear handprint was instantly visible on his cheek.

But after slapping him, Ying Chanxi, who had rushed over, was the first to burst into tears. Then, suppressing a sob, she turned her head and said, "Tingting, let's go."

With that, she turned and walked toward the intersection.

Jin Yuting hurried after her.

"Sigh... you really are something else..." The vice monitor, Shao Heqi, also chased after them hastily. Before leaving, he raised a finger and pointed at Li Luo, looking as if he was deeply disappointed in him on Ying Chanxi's behalf.

In reality, he wished he could slap the other side of Li Luo's face to make a matching pair with Ying Chanxi's handprint.

But Li Luo was a good fighter, so Shao Heqi only dared to think about it, not actually do it.

Consoling Ying Chanxi was more important right now.

"Um... Li Luo, are you okay?" Zhao Rongjun asked with some concern from the side.

Li Luo just shook his head. Though his face stung with a burning pain, such a clear sensation made the corners of his mouth unconsciously curl into a smile.

He turned to the side to look at the backs of the three people up ahead, and the scenes from his memory began to play out like a videotape, crystal clear.

Before the high school entrance exams, he and Ying Chanxi had been very close childhood friends.

They lived right across the hall from each other.

Their fathers were from the same village and were so close they had been like two peas in a pod since childhood.

Things were fine before junior high. Li Luo wasn't dumb; in elementary school, he could get good grades with minimal effort.

Although he could never beat Ying Chanxi's perfect scores in every subject, his grades were still decent.

But ever since starting junior high, where one had to study diligently to get good grades, Li Luo had become addicted to having fun. He was either playing basketball with his friends or sneaking off to an internet cafe to play games.

Compared to Ying Chanxi's, his grades were naturally worlds apart.

At home, his parents always used Ying Chanxi, the "child from next door," as an example, which annoyed Li Luo more and more until he gradually began to dislike her.

This dislike reached its peak at this juncture, the time of the high school entrance exam placements.

Because Ying Chanxi's grades were so good, she didn't even need to take the entrance exam. Over a month ago, she had already been accepted early into the best high school in the entire district through their independent admission program.

Li Luo's grades, on the other hand, were too abysmal to look at. He might not even qualify for a regular high school.

Once the entrance exams were over, Ying Chanxi would go to Yuhang Fuyi High School to receive a top-tier education. (No. 1 Affliate High School. I use pinyin for shorten)

Li Luo, however, would be forced to go to some unknown vocational high school and continue his downward slide.

From then on, they would no longer be people of the same world.

When the young Li Luo realized this, he chose to resist and escape, and in the most detestable way possible.

In contrast, after confirming her early admission, Ying Chanxi could have stopped coming to school and enjoyed an extra-long vacation.

But she still came every day, wanting to help Li Luo with his studies.

Every evening when she got home, she would also go next door to find Li Luo, wanting to help him sort through his coursework.

But to the sensitive-hearted Li Luo back then, the more Ying Chanxi did this, the more it felt like pity and charity, which he found completely unacceptable.

Especially since he knew perfectly well, what could just over a month of review possibly change?

Even if he got into a regular high school, they were destined to attend two different schools, their lives beginning to diverge.

So he gave up on himself, dragging Zhao Rongjun, who had also gotten early admission, to play basketball every day after school.

It was strange, really. How had he not thought back then that he and Zhao Rongjun would also be in different worlds in the future?

The 35-year-old Li Luo, now recalling the past, could no longer understand the thought process of his 15-year-old self.

Especially on the very last day before the entrance exams, when the school let out at noon so everyone could go home and relax, to face the next day's tests in the best possible condition.

Ying Chanxi had still been thinking that even on the last day, if she could just cram a few more formulas and vocabulary words into Li Luo's head, he might get a few more points on his exam, and maybe he could get into a regular high school.

But when she caught up to Li Luo not far from the school gate, he had impatiently shoved her away, making her fall to the ground.

Ying Chanxi, having fallen to the ground back then, must have been utterly and completely disappointed in him, right?

Thinking of this, Li Luo himself couldn't help but want to slap the other side of his own face.

"Hoo..." After finishing his recollection, Li Luo let out a long breath, calming his emotions.

Then he shoved his schoolbag into Zhao Rongjun's arms and sprinted toward the three figures ahead.

"Hey! Wait for me!" Zhao Rongjun caught Li Luo's bag and hurriedly ran after him.

At that moment, Ying Chanxi was still wiping away her tears as she walked.

The two people beside her were consoling her while cursing Li Luo.

"Chanxi, you're going to Fuyi High School from now on. No matter how much Li Luo studies, the best he can hope for is a regular high school. He might even end up in a vocational school. You won't even see him usually, so why bother with him anymore?"

Jin Yuting had long found Li Luo to be an eyesore.

Ying Chanxi was beautiful, had a good personality, and had long held the top spot in the entire school academically. She was practically a perfect goddess.

It was only when speaking with Li Luo that this polite, gentle, and outstanding girl would occasionally reveal a bit of a cute, willful side.

Countless boys at school secretly competed with each other just to get a little more of Ying Chanxi's attention.

Only that Li Luo was blind, knowing only how to play basketball and games all day, and his grades were so bad.

In Jin Yuting's eyes, only someone like Liu Shaowen, who was perennially second in their grade, tall and handsome, was a relatively good match for Chanxi.

Even the vice monitor Shao Heqi next to them, in Jin Yuting's opinion, fell a little short.

"Monitor, don't be sad anymore." Shao Heqi, who was beside them, continued to stir things up. "It's not worth being sad over someone like him. I don't think he has any intention of repenting at all."

Although it wasn't a nice thought, from Shao Heqi's perspective, Ying Chanxi having a falling out with Li Luo, especially since he'd made her cry, was actually a good thing for him.

If he could use this opportunity to console Ying Chanxi and the two of them grew closer, then later at Fuyi High School, with their junior high connection, maybe he could receive the same special treatment Li Luo had?

At this thought, Shao Heqi couldn't help but feel a little giddy.

But just then, a figure came running, reached Ying Chanxi's back, and grabbed her by the wrist.

Pulled to a halt, Ying Chanxi instinctively turned her head and saw Li Luo's face, which made her a little angry just by looking at it.

Li Luo promptly let go, his expression a little dazed.

Well... he had to admit, his teenage brain really was strange.

How could he have borne to make a girl as pretty as Ying Chanxi cry?

At this moment, tear stains still lingered on Ying Chanxi's small, oval face. Her cheeks were slightly flushed, delicate and lovely, with a touch of youthful baby fat that made one want to reach out and poke them.

Her figure was slender and slim. Even wearing the slightly bulky school uniform, it couldn't hide that pure, untainted aura about her.

But Li Luo was, after all, a 35-year-old man. After a brief moment of stunned silence, he quickly came to his senses and took a deep breath.

Before anyone else could react, Li Luo, in front of everyone, bowed slightly to Ying Chanxi and said loudly:

"Ying Chanxi, I'm sorry! I was wrong!"

"Please help me review the subjects for tomorrow's exam!"

As soon as his words fell.

Jin Yuting at the side instantly covered her mouth, her face a mask of shocked disbelief, like an old person staring at a smartphone.

The vice monitor, Shao Heqi, also let his mouth hang slightly open, his expression a mix of astonishment and confusion. He rubbed his ears, thinking he must have been hearing things.

Zhao Rongjun, who had just hurried to catch up from behind, froze in his tracks, a look of shock on his face. He stared at Li Luo's back in disbelief, almost suspecting that Li Luo had been possessed by a ghost.

And Ying Chanxi, standing in front of Li Luo, upon hearing his loud, unreserved apology and request.

Was first slightly stunned.

Then, gradually.

A light of relief and joy began to sparkle in her eyes.

"You're the one who said it."

"Of course!"
